summary: Rear range light at the inner end of Duluth's south breakwater: lit 1 Sept 1889, standing steel tower completed 1901, privately owned since a 2008 auction.

lens.where: Lake Superior Marine Museum, Duluth (LighthouseFriends; Pepper calls it the Maritime Museum)

structures.note: First rear range light, four-story wooden pyramidal tower with frame watch room; replaced by the present tower. The Board report for the year to June 1901 records transferring 'the rear beacon of the old Duluth range' to the Superior pierhead range light-station; it does not say which tower that beacon came from.

Begun June 1900, completed in August 1901 (HAER form); 67 ft (20.4 m) base to top of ventilator ball (HAER); Pepper gives 70 ft (21.3 m) from the base of the cylinder to the top of the ventilator ball

access.note: Privately owned since the 2008 auction; grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends)

facts.agency: Private owner since the 2008 online auction

events.note: Rear range light built as a wooden pyramidal tower
First exhibited the night of 1 September 1889
Steamer India smashed into the breakwater at the foot of the light on 17 Sept 1889, damaging the foundation; repaired at the owners' expense (Pepper only)
Brick oil house built for the rear range (store of 360 gallons of oil)
Fourth-order Fresnel lens made by Barbier and Benard of Paris in 1896 with six flash panels; the HAER form (1979) describes it in the lantern. Installation date not given.
Present steel skeletal tower begun June 1900 and completed August 1901 (HAER form); Pepper dates the iron work's delivery to summer 1901
Board report for the year to June 1901 records transferring 'the rear beacon of the old Duluth range' to the Superior pierhead range light-station; the tower it came from is not stated.
Commissioner's 1922 list: electric incandescent from incandescent oil vapor; Bulletin index 1918-1923 lists a change in illuminant
Fourth-order optic replaced by a modern acrylic optic; the Fresnel and its pedestal went to a maritime museum (Pepper)
Deemed excess by the Coast Guard; offered at no cost to eligible entities in May 2007
Online auction closed 2 December 2008 with the lighthouse sold to private buyers for $31,000

corrections.why: The standing steel skeletal tower was begun in 1900 and completed in August 1901 (NRHP). The 1889 date belongs to the wooden tower it replaced.

corrections.proposed: Private owner since the 2008 online auction
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends reports the Coast Guard declared the inner light excess in 2007, sold it at auction in 2008, and says it is privately owned.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's first-year conflict is between the 1889 wooden rear light and the standing steel tower of 1900 to 1901. Both are real; the record's 1889 date describes the first tower, the standing structure is 1901. Pepper dates the start of the iron work to summer 1901, against June 1900 in the NRHP.
The NRHP gives 67 ft to the top of the ventilator ball and Pepper gives 70 ft for the same tower; the record's 20.5 m falls between them.

LighthouseFriends dates a seven-room keeper's dwelling to 1873 and places the head keeper in the 1873 dwelling when the new lights were lit in 1901. Pepper calls the crew's only dwelling a small frame house built for the keeper in 1874. Not resolved; the story states both.

HAER gives June 1900 as the start of the present structure and August 1901 as its completion. Pepper says the iron work was delivered in summer 1901 and that work began then with the foundation blocks. The Board report for the year to June 1901 already describes 'the iron beacon now being built'. Not resolved.

notes_for_editor: KEEPERS: the USLHS place record is 'Duluth Harbor North Breakwater' (established 1910) and does not say which Duluth light each man served. LighthouseFriends' keeper line for this light prints the same head keepers (Jefferson 1873-1888 through Bannan 1970), which is the only source tying the list to this station; the story says so. Roster lines are attached without person slugs. Post-1960 Coast Guard names are carried as the archive prints them and are not repeated in the story text. NARA registers not checked. SOURCE 1: the cached file at npgallery 83000945.pdf is a two-page HAER inventory form (Charles K. Hyde, 1979), not the NRHP nomination; it is cited as the HAER form. WIKIPEDIA: consulted for leads only, not cited. PRIVATE BUYERS: LighthouseFriends names the 2008 buyers; they are private individuals and are not named. INDEX SPLIT: the Bulletin index entry says 'change in illuminant' without a year; the story says 'By 1922' from the Commissioner's 1922 list. STEAMER INDIA: appears only in Pepper's history; no Minnesota newspaper page found. CURRENT CHARACTERISTIC: the record's Fl W 5s is not confirmed by any source read. LENS: LighthouseFriends (1889 Barbier & Fenestre, ten panels) and Pepper (single flash) describe the first optic differently; the HAER form gives the 1896 Barbier & Benard optic, and which lens the museum holds is not settled. PAGES CHECKED against the corpus page index: Board 1894 p.526, Board 1901 p.243, Commissioner 1922 p.731, Bulletin index PDF p.11. SIBLING STORY: data/stories/us-mn-duluth-south-breakwater-outer.md covers the outer light and the same canal crew; check its keeper framing against this record before both go live. LENGTH: the story body is shorter than the rich band because the Board reports for 1889 and 1890 are not in the corpus, the 1902 to 1915 operating record is thin, and the storm record rests on one Pepper entry.
